title: Underworld: Rise of the Lycans
full_review:
"Underworld: Rise of the Lycans" (Screen Gems), the third installment in the horror action franchise, uses the saga of a slave revolt as an excuse for mindless bloodletting.

Set close to 1,000 years before the action of the previous films -- 2003's "Underworld" and 2006's "Underworld: Evolution" -- this prequel follows the adventures of Lucian (Michael Sheen), the first of a race of part-human, part-werewolf creatures called Lycans.

Although treated as a protege by the cruel vampire King Viktor (Bill Nighy), Lucian, a bit like Moses in the Exodus story, increasingly sides with his oppressed fellow Lycans, whom the vampires, realizing their potential strength, have subsequently bred as slaves.

Lucian's dealings with Viktor are further complicated by his forbidden romance with the sovereign's much-loved but independent-minded daughter Sonja (Rhona Mitra).

Director Patrick Tatopolous, who designed and supervised the first film's creatures and served as production designer for the second, now takes the helm in his feature debut. But a potentially intriguing story line and Nighy's aristocratic brand of villainy are swamped in a rising tide of gory mayhem.

The film contains pervasive violence, much of it with gore, torture and nongraphic premarital sexual activity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
